h1: What Does a Financial Consultancy Firm Do in Nepal?
directAnswer: A financial consultancy firm in Nepal provides forward-looking advisory services that help businesses and individuals structure budgets, optimize operating cash flows, manage working capital, and maintain statutory compliance. Unlike traditional bookkeepers who record historical data or statutory auditors who perform post-year compliance audits, financial consultants guide strategic decisions to drive long-term profitability and financial resilience.
author: Lalitpur Advisory Research Desk

sections.h2: Core Services Offered by Financial Consultants in Nepal
sections.contentHtml:
In Nepal's rapidly developing commercial landscape, managing business finances requires more than simple voucher entry. Professional financial consultants provide four primary categories of high-impact strategic advisory:

1. Cash Flow & Working Capital Advisory

Designing rolling 13-week cash-flow projections, managing supplier credit terms, and optimizing inventory holding to prevent liquidity crunches during festival cycles like Dashain.

2. Strategic Budgeting & Forecasting

Formulating annual operational budgets, scenario-testing revenue models, and establishing department-level spending ceilings.

3. Capital Structuring & Bank Proposals

Drafting Detailed Project Reports (DPR), calculating Debt Service Coverage Ratios (DSCR), and structuring collateral documentation for commercial bank lending.

4. Internal Controls & Audit Readiness

Establishing double-entry chart of accounts, maker-checker authorization protocols, and pre-audit file reconciliation before statutory submission.

sections.h2: Consultant vs. Accountant vs. Auditor: Clear Distinctions
sections.contentHtml:
A common misconception in Kathmandu and Lalitpur is conflating financial consultants with accountants and auditors. In Nepal, each professional performs distinct statutory and operational functions:

RolePrimary Time HorizonCore DeliverableRegulatory Mandate
Financial ConsultantFuture (Forecasts & Projections)Cash-flow models, budgets, bank proposalsManagement advisory contract
Internal Accountant / BookkeeperPast & Present (Daily transactions)Day-to-day ledgers, VAT books, trial balanceInternal operations
Statutory Auditor (ICAN)Historical (Closed fiscal year)Independent Audit Report & OpinionNepal Chartered Accountants Act 2053

sections.h2: When Should Your Organization Engage a Consultant?
sections.contentHtml: Engaging a financial consultancy is recommended during inflection points: launching a new company, scaling past NPR 50 Lakhs in annual turnover, preparing for equity fundraising, or managing persistent cash-flow bottlenecks. Learn more about our specialized financial consultancy services in Nepal.

faqs.question: Can a financial consultancy in Nepal conduct our statutory audit?
faqs.answer: No. Under the Nepal Chartered Accountants Act 2053, statutory audits can only be executed and signed by licensed Chartered Accountants or Registered Auditors registered with the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nepal (ICAN). A financial consultancy prepares ledgers and coordinates with your auditor, but cannot issue an independent audit opinion.

faqs.question: Does financial consultancy include tax filing assistance?
faqs.answer: Yes, financial consultants assist with tax planning, record organization, and advance tax computation, helping ensure clean data submission to the Inland Revenue Department (IRD).
